body.statement:
\textbf{Repaired rare-margin sharpness question.}
Fix a boundary sequence with \(\kappa_n\downarrow0\), \(n\kappa_n\to\infty\), and \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}n\kappa_n^3<\infty\).  First determine a minimal faithful uniform regularity condition on a subclass of \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) that excludes the response-boundary counterexample by controlling response interiority, nondegenerate response variance, relative variance consistency, or Gaussian anti-concentration.  The condition must be stated in primitive terms and must not assume the desired quantile or coverage conclusion.  Only on the resulting repaired subclass, and after the companion sufficiency question is posed on that same subclass, determine whether \(n\kappa_n^3\) is a sharp threshold for rare-margin optimal-face switching by establishing or refuting
\[
\forall t=(t_n)_{n\geq1}\ \text{with }t_n>0\text{ and }t_n\to0,
\quad
\exists\mathbb P^{(t)}\in\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}
\ \text{satisfying the selected regularity condition}:
\quad
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\Pr_{\mathbb P^{(t)}}\!\left(
[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)
\right)<1-\alpha.
\]
Use the two schedule-dependent branches in \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{unif}}\) on the \(2\times2\) array with \(p_n=r_n=(\kappa_n,1-\kappa_n)\) and \(\Delta_n\) zero or local at rate \((n\kappa_n)^{-1/2}\).  Any negative conclusion must exhibit an actual critical-value or coverage distortion caused by rare-margin face switching rather than response-variance collapse.  The question concerns only this paired numerical-delta procedure and makes no minimax impossibility claim for other confidence procedures.
body.justification: This is the procedural-sharpness half of the headline frontier and has the required for-every-schedule, there-exists-experiment quantifiers.
body.gap: Existing uniform LP confidence methods show that a failure of this particular tuning scheme would not imply impossibility of uniform inference. The unresolved issue is whether the proposed numerical-delta implementation has the stated rare-cell threshold.
body.consumer: A matching failure theorem would tell practitioners when changing the numerical step cannot rescue this paired endpoint implementation even though rare-cell information still diverges.

obligation.what_is_open: Characterize a minimal primitive uniform response-nondegeneracy or anti-concentration condition that excludes the response-boundary array without assuming coverage, and then determine whether bounded \(n\kappa_n^3\) forces schedule-quantified undercoverage through rare-margin optimal-face switching on that repaired subclass.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian and multiplier approximations control absolute weak distance but impose no response-interiority, variance lower bound, relative variance consistency, or quantile anti-concentration.  They therefore allow a degenerate Gaussian limit and an atom at the limiting critical value, for which vanishing-width intervals miss an \(n^{-1}\)-scale ridge discrepancy with nonvanishing probability.
obligation.attempted: The two-context all-zero-event construction was evaluated for every positive numerical-delta schedule.  It proves genuine critical-value and coverage distortion, but that distortion persists independently of rare margins and so cannot certify procedural sharpness of the \(n\kappa_n^3\) boundary.  Reusing it as a rare-margin witness would misattribute the mechanism.
obligation.partial_result:
The all-zero response construction gives one fixed experiment \(\mathbb P^0\), independent of \(t\), for which both singleton-uniform bounded-Lipschitz approximation statements hold but
\[
\forall t=(t_n)_{n\geq1}\ \text{with }t_n>0,qquad
\limsup_{n\to\infty}
\Pr_{\mathbb P^0}\!\left(
[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)
\right)
\leq1-\exp(-\lambda)<1-\alpha.
\]
This proves response-boundary failure but does not determine the rare-margin \(n\kappa_n^3\) threshold after response nondegeneracy is imposed.
